perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information/subjective perspective:

- He and Jonathan Balogun have been close friends since childhood. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice on personal and professional matters and values Jonathan’s more educated perspective.
- Christian had felt Jonathan was acting differently and hiding something important. This made Christian anxious and suspicious, so he arranged to meet Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. Jonathan admitted he had been keeping something from Christian and said he was in some trouble and hadn’t known how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic and offered to help. Jonathan told him the situation was complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. Jonathan told him he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he himself didn’t do anything illegal.
- Christian decided to look into the matter discreetly to make sure Jonathan was safe. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted him to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian learned/believed Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this, said he wasn’t sure yet who was responsible but had leads, and planned to gather more evidence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later found out/believed the person behind it was someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He planned to confront that person and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous and said he trusted Christian to do what was right.
- The specific identity/name of the culprit is not disclosed in the provided dialogue, though Christian believes he has found out who it is.
